works: A Prisoner taken after the defeat of the Rebels at Sedgemore, 1685. "The Earl of Feversham ordered twentytwo of the prisoners to be hanged on the spot . . . The person who was remarkably swift of foot was prevailed upon, on condition of being pardoned, to entertain the General with an instance of his agility ; accordingly, having stripped himself naked, a halter was put round his neck, and the opposite end was fastened to the neck of a horse. Death of the son of Prince Platoff, in a charge of cavalry which took place at Vereia, in Russia, in the campaign of 181 2; from Labaume. " Platoff, who saw his best soldiers falling around him, forgot his own danger, and with an anxious eye looked round for his favourite son; but the hour approached when this unfortunate father was destined to feel that life is sometimes almost insupportable. The unhappy youth had returned from the heat of the battle, and was preparing to renew the attack, when he received a mortal wound from a Hulan Pole. At this moment his father appeared, and flying to his assistance threw himself upon him. On seeing his beloved parent, the son heaved a deep sigh, and would have expressed for the last time his affection and his duty, but as he attempted to speak, his strength failed him, and he breathed his last."
